title.source: Play-Doh：擦牆膏怎麼變成玩具？｜品牌故事
title.text: Play-Doh: How Did Wallpaper Cleaner Become a Toy? | Brand Story

description.source:
一團原本擦壁紙的材料，怎麼換成孩子手上的玩具，又走向成人花藝？循著Kutol的公司史、The Strong的歷史回顧、美國專利，以及孩之寶的產品公告，看使用者如何改變顏色、工具與保存要求。1956是公司回顧的品牌生日；後來專利與現代套件各有自己的年代和產品範圍。匿名概念插圖不重建歷史現場。

description.text:
How did a compound once used to clean wallpaper become a child's toy, then enter adult floral crafting? Follow Kutol's company history, The Strong's historical accounts, a U.S. patent and Hasbro's product announcements to see how users changed the demands on colors, tools and storage. 1956 is the brand's birthday in the company's retrospective; the later patent and modern kits each belong to their own period and product scope. Anonymous conceptual illustrations do not reconstruct historical scenes.

lines.source: 如果你捏的形狀，手一放就垮，還會再拿這罐嗎？
lines.text: If the shape you made collapsed the moment you let go, would you reach for this can again?

lines.source: 孩之寶二〇二四年說，Play-Doh年出貨逾五億罐。
lines.text: In 2024, Hasbro said Play-Doh shipped more than 500 million cans a year.

lines.source: 想像你在一九五〇年代的辛辛那提，正打開一罐壁紙清潔材料。
lines.text: Imagine opening a can of wallpaper cleaner in Cincinnati in the 1950s.

lines.source: 但在你眼前，牆上的煤灰正在變少。你取出材料，手感還好好的，卻得找個理由，
lines.text: But in front of you, there's less soot on the walls. You take out the compound. It still feels fine, but you need a reason

lines.source: 讓人再次打開這罐。
lines.text: for someone to open this can again.

lines.source: 我覺得最棘手的，是材料還能用，原本的工作卻正在縮小。
lines.text: To me, that's the hardest part: the material still works, but its old job is shrinking.

lines.source: 有一雙更小的手，正被另一團材料難住。
lines.text: A smaller pair of hands is struggling with a different lump of material.

lines.source: 另一張桌上，一束剛做完的花，還得過最後一關。
lines.text: On another table, a newly made bunch of flowers still faces one last test.

lines.source: 今天跟著Play-Doh，追一團材料怎麼在不同人的手上留下來。
lines.text: Today, we'll follow Play-Doh to see how one compound finds a place in different people's hands.

lines.source: 拿它的手換了，它究竟要替那個人做對什麼？
lines.text: When those hands change, what does it need to do right for the person holding it?

lines.source: 開場那罐材料，得先接到一份清潔訂單。史壯玩具博物館把故事的這一步，
lines.text: First, that can from our opening needed an order for cleaning supplies. The Strong museum dates this step in the story

lines.source: 放在一九三三年。
克里奧・麥克維克替Kutol接下克羅格的生意，要做現成的壁紙清潔材料，放到商店裡賣。
lines.text: Cleo McVicker secured business from Kroger for Kutol: make a ready-to-use wallpaper cleaner to sell in stores.

lines.source: 麻煩的是，館方說他們以前沒做過這種東西。訂單到手了，誰把材料做出來？
lines.text: The catch, the museum says, was that they'd never made anything like it. With the order secured, who would make the compound?

lines.source: 依這篇回顧，負責產品開發的兄弟諾亞拿出了配方；柔軟、像黏土的清潔材料，
lines.text: According to this account, his brother Noah, who handled product development, came up with the formula. A soft, clay-like cleaner

lines.source: 就接上了這份工作。
lines.text: was put to work.

lines.source: 如果你家牆面沾了煤灰，手裡這團能變形的材料，就有了一個要處理的目標：
lines.text: If your walls were covered in soot, that moldable lump in your hand now had something to tackle:

lines.source: 牆上那層髒污。
lines.text: the grime on the wallpaper.

lines.source: 想像你把它攤開，再收回手心；你在意的是，手上這次動作，能不能讓那片壁紙好看一點。
lines.text: Imagine spreading it out, then gathering it back into your palm. What matters to you is whether that motion makes the wallpaper look a little better.

lines.source: 我覺得，這時候你需要留下的，是剛才那團形狀嗎？
lines.text: I wonder: at this point, do you need to preserve the shape you just made?

lines.source: 牆面乾淨，這個動作就能收手；手裡的外形，只是過程。
lines.text: Once the wall is clean, you can stop. The shape in your hand was just part of the process.

lines.source: 館方接著記下，一九四九年克里奧去世，兒子約瑟夫接手了生意。
lines.text: The museum then records Cleo's death in 1949. His son Joseph took over the business.

lines.source: 輪到他想辦法讓公司繼續做下去。
lines.text: It was his turn to work out how to keep the company going.

lines.source: 但一筆生意，能不能只靠原來那面牆，一直做下去？
lines.text: But could a business keep going with nothing but that same old wall?

lines.source: 回到開場那面煤灰變少的牆：館方說，二戰後家庭改用燃油或天然氣，到了五〇年代初，
lines.text: Back to the wall with less soot from our opening: the museum says households switched to oil or natural gas after World War II. By the early 1950s,

lines.source: 壁紙清潔材料的銷售開始下滑。
lines.text: sales of wallpaper cleaner had begun to fall.

lines.source: 如果你家的煤灰問題少了，這罐東西就可能留在櫃子裡；它做得到原來的工作，
lines.text: If soot was less of a problem in your home, this can might stay in the cupboard. It could still do its old job,

lines.source: 也未必等得到你再買一罐。
lines.text: but that didn't mean you'd buy another one.

lines.source: 你若接住約瑟夫手上的材料，會讓它去見誰？
lines.text: If you took that compound from Joseph's hands, who would you introduce it to?

lines.source: 有沒有一雙手，根本不打算拿它擦牆？
lines.text: Were there hands that had no intention of cleaning walls with it?

lines.source: 這雙不想擦牆的手，來自幼稚園。Kutol的公司史裡，老師凱・祖法爾是約瑟夫的姻親。
lines.text: Those hands were in a kindergarten. In Kutol's company history, the teacher, Kay Zufall, was related to Joseph by marriage.

lines.source: 博物館把她提出手工用途，放在一九五五年。還記得開場那雙小手嗎？
lines.text: The museum dates her suggestion of a craft use to 1955. Remember those little hands from the opening?

lines.source: 名人堂說，一般塑形黏土太硬，孩子不好操作。
lines.text: The Toy Hall of Fame says ordinary modeling clay was too stiff for children to handle easily.

lines.source: 想像你要做一隻小動物，連身體都壓不出來，耳朵怎麼接？
lines.text: Imagine trying to make a little animal. If you can't even press out its body, how will you attach its ears?

lines.source: 作品還沒出現，手就先被難住了。
lines.text: Before a creation can take shape, your hands are already struggling.

lines.source: 名人堂回顧，約瑟夫送材料讓老師試；Kutol記下她把它帶進幼稚園，受到了歡迎。清潔材料，
lines.text: The Hall of Fame recounts Joseph sending the teacher some compound to try. Kutol records her taking it into kindergarten, where it was a hit. A cleaner

lines.source: 碰上了要塑形的小手。
lines.text: had met little hands that wanted to shape things.

lines.source: 換到容易推動的材料，你可以先壓一個身體，再接上一對耳朵；這樣的用途，
lines.text: With a compound that's easier to move, you can press out a body, then add a pair of ears. But did the person running the business

lines.source: 有沒有真的讓經營者看見？
lines.text: actually see that use for himself?

lines.source: 博物館接著寫，約瑟夫到學校看了孩子的作品，回去把產品重新調整、改作玩具，
lines.text: The museum goes on to say that Joseph visited the school to see the children's creations. He then reworked the product as a toy,

lines.source: 使用原有的設備和製造空間。
lines.text: using the existing equipment and manufacturing space.

lines.source: 我喜歡這個具體的來回：他到桌邊看做出了什麼，再把這種用途帶回製造的地方，
lines.text: I like that concrete back-and-forth: he went to the table to see what they'd made, then brought that use back to the factory.

lines.source: 材料的評分方式已經變了。
lines.text: The criteria for judging the compound had changed.

lines.source: 教室願意用，下一步由誰把它當玩具來做？
lines.text: The classroom wanted it. Who would make it as a toy next?

lines.source: 館方把Rainbow Crafts的成立，放在一九五六年。
lines.text: The museum dates the founding of Rainbow Crafts to 1956.

lines.source: 那是Kutol的子公司，向辛辛那提一帶的小學推廣Play-Doh；
lines.text: It was a Kutol subsidiary that promoted Play-Doh to elementary schools around Cincinnati.

lines.source: 孩之寶也把品牌的誕生放在這一年。
lines.text: Hasbro also places the brand's birth in that year.

lines.source: 但你做出一隻鳥，還想替它選嘴巴的顏色，只有原來那一團，夠不夠？
lines.text: But if you've made a bird and want to choose a color for its beak, is that original lump enough?

lines.source: 一九五七年，館方記下紅、黃、藍加入；名人堂的回顧還提到，材料變得更柔軟。
